title: Running Work Orders per Customer and Work Order References
content:
# Desk Standing Rule: Running Work Orders per Customer and Work Order References

A customer of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service may have several pieces at the bench at once. Across the service as a whole one customer may have at most 8 work orders running at one time, and each service level caps how many of its own work orders may run for that customer at a time; the cap at each level is the level's own figure.

## 1. The opening condition

A further work order is opened at a service level only when no work order already recorded against the same work order reference stands at intake, estimated, awaiting authorization, in workshop or ready for pickup.

## 2. What the condition is read from

The condition is read from the records before the order is opened, not from what the customer recalls. What is looked at is the work order reference the new order would be recorded against, the work orders already standing against that reference, and the state each of them stands at. An order counts against the condition while it stands at any of the five states named in clause 1; an order that has been delivered, returned unrepaired, cancelled or treated as abandoned does not.

## 3. Where the cap at the level is reached

Where the cap at the service level is reached the piece is either taken in at another service level that admits it, or held until a running order closes, and the customer is told which of the two applies.

## Points of judgement

| The records show | The condition in clause 1 |
|---|---|
| No work order against that reference | met |
| One work order against that reference standing at intake | not met |
| One against that reference standing ready for pickup | not met |
| One against that reference delivered last month | met |
| One against that reference cancelled before pricing | met |

## A hypothetical case

A customer has four work orders running at Standard Bench Service, which caps its own running orders at that level's figure, and brings in a fifth piece. Where the level's cap is reached, the two courses in clause 3 are the ones open: the piece is taken in at another level that admits it, or it is held until one of the running orders closes, and the customer is told which applies.
